# Psychoacoustic Metrics Index

> An index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance), organised by the standard edition or model each implementation follows. All programming languages.

Data as of 2026-10-06. 22 methods, 1 project, languages: C, Python. Each implementation is tied to the standard edition or model paper it follows, with its validation evidence as stated by the project. Repository and package metadata are refreshed weekly.

## Loudness

- [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.md): current edition ISO 532-1:2017; implementations: MetaSona
- [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.md): current edition ISO 532-2:2017; implementations: none found
- [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.md): current edition ISO 532-3:2023; implementations: none found
- [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona

## Sharpness

- [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.md): current edition DIN 45692:2009; implementations: MetaSona

## Roughness

- [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.md): current edition Daniel & Weber (1997); implementations: MetaSona
- [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona
- [Roughness, DIN 38455](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-din-38455.md): current edition DIN 38455:2024; implementations: none found

## Fluctuation strength

- [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.md): current edition Osses et al. (2016); implementations: none found
- [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: none found

## Tonality

- [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.md): current edition Aures (1985b); implementations: MetaSona
- [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.md): current edition ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.); implementations: MetaSona
- [Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.md): current edition ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.); implementations: none found
- [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.md): current edition DIN 45681:2005; implementations: none found
- [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.md): current edition ISO/TS 20065:2022; implementations: none found
- [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.md): current edition ISO 1996-2:2017; implementations: none found
- [Tonal audibility of wind turbine noise (IEC 61400-11)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iec-61400-11.md): current edition IEC 61400-11:2012+AMD1:2018; implementations: none found

## Impulsiveness

- [Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.md): current edition ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022; implementations: none found

## Psychoacoustic annoyance

- [Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.md): current edition Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016); implementations: none found

# About this index

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/about.html

An index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics (loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness and psychoacoustic annoyance), organised by the standard edition or model each implementation follows. All programming languages.

## What is included

Open-source code that computes a psychoacoustic metric and says which model or standard edition it follows. Quantities: loudness, sharpness, roughness, fluctuation strength, tonality, impulsiveness, psychoacoustic annoyance, and related quantities. Not included: LUFS / ITU-R BS.1770, speech intelligibility, codec quality metrics (PEAQ, PESQ, ViSQOL), psychophysics experiment software and closed-source tools. Reference programs that are free to download but not open source (such as the ISO 532 programs) are listed and marked.

## How entries are checked

Each entry is written from the project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The index records what a project claims; it does not run the code. Repository dates, releases and package versions are refreshed every week by a GitHub Action, which also searches for new candidate projects and watches the standards bodies for new editions. A person reviews the findings before anything is added.

## Status of an implementation

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| available | In the latest release, or on the default branch of a project without releases. |
| unreleased | Merged on the default branch but newer than the latest release. |
| proposed | Open pull request or separate branch, not merged. |

## Validation evidence

As stated by each project:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| standard or paper data | Compared with test signals or values published in the standard or the model paper. |
| reference code | Compared with the reference program or the model authors' own code. |
| another implementation | Compared with another independent implementation. |
| own tests only | Tests exist, but without external reference data. |
| not stated | The project does not say how it was validated. |

## Machine-readable data

- [index.json](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/index.json): the whole index as JSON
- [llms.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/llms.txt) and [llms-full.txt](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/llms-full.txt): summaries for language models
- [feed.xml](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/feed.xml): Atom feed of updates
- Source data and schema: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/tree/main/data

## Contributing and citing

Corrections and new projects are welcome through issues or pull requests: https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index. To cite the index, use the CITATION.cff file in the repository. Maintained by Zhenxian Li. Licence: MIT.

# Frequently asked questions

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/faq.html

## Which psychoacoustic metrics can I compute in Python?

Current editions of 7 methods have an available implementation that can be called from Python: [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html), and [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html). Projects: MetaSona.

## Which psychoacoustic metrics can I compute in C/C++?

Current editions of 7 methods have an available implementation that can be called from C/C++: [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html), [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html), and [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html). Projects: MetaSona.

## Which open-source code implements Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)?

The current edition is ISO 532-1:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-1. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels).

## Which open-source code implements Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)?

The current edition is ISO 532-2:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-2. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)?

The current edition is ISO 532-3:2023. In development: ISO/CD 532-3. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo).

## Which open-source code implements sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)?

The current edition is DIN 45692:2009. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; from specific loudness).

## Which open-source code implements roughness, Daniel & Weber model?

There is no standard; the reference model is Daniel & Weber (1997). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C).

## Which open-source code implements roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied).

## Which open-source code implements roughness, DIN 38455?

The current edition is DIN 38455:2024. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula?

There is no standard; the reference model is Osses et al. (2016). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements tonality, Aures/Terhardt model?

There is no standard; the reference model is Aures (1985b). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C).

## Which open-source code implements tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)?

The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo).

The current edition is ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

There is no standard; the reference models are Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016). In development: ISO/AWI 26573. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Which open-source code implements equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)?

The current edition is ISO 226:2023. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

The current edition is ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Why does it matter which edition a tool implements?

Psychoacoustic standards change between editions. ECMA-418-2, for example, has had four editions since 2020 that changed the hearing model, roughness and loudness, and all three parts of ISO 532 are being revised. Two tools that both claim to implement a standard can therefore give different values for the same sound. Each method page lists the editions and which tool follows which.

## How are the entries checked?

From each project's own README, documentation, release notes, licence file and package metadata, with links to those sources. The index records what a project claims and does not run the code. Repository and package metadata are refreshed every week, and a person reviews new findings.

# Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-1, ISO 532B, ISO 532 method B, DIN 45631, DIN 45631/A1, Zwicker method, N5, percentile loudness

Loudness from Zwicker's model: third-octave band levels are turned into specific loudness on the critical-band (Bark) scale and integrated. ISO 532-1:2017 specifies one procedure for stationary sounds and one for time-varying sounds (from which percentile values such as N5 are taken), and replaced method B of ISO 532:1975. The German standards DIN 45631 (stationary) and DIN 45631/A1 (time-varying) describe the same method.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-1:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-1. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/90809.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-1:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Stationary and time-varying procedures; Annex A reference program, Annex B test signals. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 2010-03 | [DIN 45631/A1:2010](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084) | current | Adds the procedure for time-varying sounds. | — |
| 1991-03 | [DIN 45631:1991](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531) | current | Stationary sounds. | — |
| 1975-07 | [ISO 532:1975](https://www.iso.org/standard/4603.html) | withdrawn | Method B (Zwicker) for stationary sounds, from third-octave levels. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | ISO 532-1:2017 — stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Model tables taken from MoSQITo and checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24. |

**See also:** [Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. ISO 532:1975. Acoustics — Method for calculating loudness level. https://www.iso.org/standard/4603.html
2. DIN 45631:1991. Berechnung des Lautstärkepegels und der Lautheit aus dem Geräuschspektrum; Verfahren nach E. Zwicker. https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631/1666531
3. DIN 45631/A1:2010. Calculation of loudness level and loudness from the sound spectrum — Zwicker method — Amendment 1: Calculation of the loudness of time-variant sound. https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45631-a1/122476084
4. ISO 532-1:2017. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 1: Zwicker method. https://www.iso.org/standard/63077.html
5. ISO/CD 532-1. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 1: Zwicker method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90809.html

# Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4, ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007, Moore-Glasberg method, Cambridge loudness model

Loudness of stationary sounds from the Moore–Glasberg model: the spectrum is turned into an excitation pattern on the ERB-number scale, then into specific loudness, which is summed. ANSI S3.4-2007 standardised the model of Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) with later modifications; ISO 532-2:2017 specifies the method for monaural and binaural listening.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-2:2017. In development: ISO/CD 532-2. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-2](https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2017-06 | [ISO 532-2:2017](https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Monaural and binaural loudness of stationary sounds; source code supplied with the standard. | — |
| 2011 | [Chen et al. (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001) | published | Faster excitation-pattern calculation, also for hearing loss (not standardised). | — |
| 2007 | [ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020) | current | American standard based on the 1997 model with later modifications. | — |
| 1997 | Moore, Glasberg & Baer (1997) | published | Model paper (thresholds, loudness and partial loudness). | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html)

## References

1. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., & Baer, T. (1997). A model for the prediction of thresholds, loudness, and partial loudness. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 45(4), 224–240.
2. ANSI/ASA S3.4-2007. Procedure for the Computation of Loudness of Steady Sounds. https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/asa/ANSIASAS32007R2020
3. Chen, Z., Hu, G., Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2011). A new method of calculating auditory excitation patterns and loudness for steady sounds. *Hearing Research*, 282(1–2), 204–215. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.heares.2011.08.001
4. ISO 532-2:2017. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method. https://www.iso.org/standard/63078.html
5. ISO/CD 532-2. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 2: Moore-Glasberg method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90812.html

# Time-varying loudness, Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher (ISO 532-3)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg-time-varying.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone, phon · **Also known as:** ISO 532-3, TVL, time-varying loudness, Glasberg and Moore 2002, Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method, short-term loudness, long-term loudness

Loudness of time-varying sounds as instantaneous, short-term and long-term loudness. It starts from the Glasberg & Moore (2002) model; Moore et al. (2016) added binaural inhibition and Moore et al. (2018) revised the time constants. ISO 532-3:2023 standardises the resulting Moore–Glasberg–Schlittenlacher method for stationary and time-varying sounds.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO 532-3:2023. In development: ISO/CD 532-3. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [ISO/CD 532-3](https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html) | in development | Second edition at committee-draft stage since November 2024. | — |
| 2023-07 | [ISO 532-3:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html) | current; Under revision; the 2nd edition has been at committee-draft stage since 2024-11-01. | Standardised method; source code supplied with the standard. | — |
| 2018 | [Moore et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246) | published | Revised time constants. | — |
| 2016 | [Moore et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698) | published | Adds binaural inhibition. | — |
| 2002 | Glasberg & Moore (2002) | published | Time-varying loudness model (short-term and long-term loudness). | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Moore–Glasberg loudness of stationary sounds (ISO 532-2, ANSI S3.4)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-moore-glasberg.html)

## References

1. Glasberg, B. R., & Moore, B. C. J. (2002). A model of loudness applicable to time-varying sounds. *Journal of the Audio Engineering Society*, 50(5), 331–342.
2. Moore, B. C. J., Glasberg, B. R., Varathanathan, A., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2016). A loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *Trends in Hearing*, 20, 2331216516682698. https://doi.org/10.1177/2331216516682698
3. Moore, B. C. J., Jervis, M., Harries, L., & Schlittenlacher, J. (2018). Testing and refining a loudness model for time-varying sounds incorporating binaural inhibition. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 143(3), 1504–1513. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.5027246
4. ISO 532-3:2023. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method. https://www.iso.org/standard/69856.html
5. ISO/CD 532-3. Acoustics — Methods for calculating loudness — Part 3: Moore-Glasberg-Schlittenlacher method (2nd edition). https://www.iso.org/standard/90816.html

# Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Loudness · **Unit:** sone_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 loudness, Sottek Hearing Model, SHM loudness, sone_HMS, hearing model loudness

Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model defined in ECMA-418-2. The hearing model (Clause 5) produces specific loudness; the 2nd edition (2022) added a loudness calculation for sounds with tonal and noise components (Clause 8). ECMA-418-2 has had four editions in five years, so implementations of different editions can disagree.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model clauses 5.1.2.2 and 5.1.5.2 revised; conformance requires 48 kHz sampling. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Adds a diffuse-field outer and middle ear filter. | — |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | New Clause 8, loudness of sounds with subcritical or wider bandwidth. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Hearing model (Clause 5) with specific loudness. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) — Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo | `loudness_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | another implementation | since 0.2.0; Adapted from the SQAT/RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen. |

**See also:** [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html), [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html)

2. ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf

# Sharpness (DIN 45692, Aures, von Bismarck)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html

**Quantity:** Sharpness · **Unit:** acum · **Also known as:** DIN 45692, acum, Zwicker sharpness, Aures sharpness, von Bismarck sharpness

Sharpness is the weighted first moment of specific loudness along the critical-band rate, with a weighting that emphasises high frequencies. DIN 45692:2009 standardises the weighting and a test procedure, using Zwicker specific loudness (ISO 532-1 / DIN 45631). Most implementations also offer the weightings of von Bismarck (1974) and Aures (1985).

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 45692:2009. Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; from specific loudness).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2009-08 | [DIN 45692:2009](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111) | current | Standardised weighting and test procedure; no revision announced. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 1985 | Aures (1985b) | published | Weighting that depends on total loudness. | — |
| 1974 | von Bismarck (1974) | published | Original sharpness weighting. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | DIN 45692:2009 — from specific loudness | `sharpness_din45692` | not stated | since 0.1.0 |

**See also:** [Zwicker loudness (ISO 532-1, DIN 45631)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html)

## References

1. von Bismarck, G. (1974). Sharpness as an attribute of the timbre of steady sounds. *Acustica*, 30(3), 159–172.
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.
3. DIN 45692:2009. Messtechnische Simulation der Hörempfindung Schärfe (Measurement technique for the simulation of the auditory sensation of sharpness). https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-45692/117635111

# Roughness, Daniel & Weber model

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** Daniel and Weber roughness, Daniel & Weber 1997, Aures roughness, asper

Roughness from the model of Daniel & Weber (1997), an optimised version of Aures's (1985) model. It is not standardised, and the paper leaves details open (filter bank, calibration, framing), so implementations can give different values for the same signal.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Daniel & Weber (1997). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C).

SQAT replaced its implementation in September 2026 with one that follows Dik Hermes's code, which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1997 | Daniel & Weber (1997) | published | Reference model. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 1985 | Aures (1985a) | published | Earlier model that Daniel & Weber optimised. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | Daniel & Weber (1997) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Aures, W. (1985). Ein Berechnungsverfahren der Rauhigkeit [A procedure for calculating auditory roughness]. *Acustica*, 58, 268–281.
2. Daniel, P., & Weber, R. (1997). Psychoacoustical roughness: Implementation of an optimized model. *Acta Acustica united with Acustica*, 83(1), 113–123.

# Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 roughness, asper_HMS, Sottek roughness, SHM roughness

Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 7 of ECMA-418-2. The 2nd edition (2022) added an optional entropy weighting for cases where rotational speed is measured; the 3rd edition (2024) changed zero-padding and segmentation, the largest change to roughness so far.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied).

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Zero-padding and segmentation adapted; main revision of roughness. | — |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation; optional entropy-weighted roughness. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 7 roughness. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) — mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied | `roughness_ecma` | another implementation | since 0.2.0; Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |

**See also:** [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
2. ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (models based on human perception). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf

4. ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 2 (methods for describing human perception based on the Sottek Hearing Model). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf

# Roughness, DIN 38455

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-din-38455.html

**Quantity:** Roughness · **Unit:** asper · **Also known as:** DIN 38455, Rauigkeit, German roughness standard

DIN 38455:2024 is the first German standard for calculating roughness. Its text is not freely available, and the model it specifies could not be confirmed from public sources; a hearing-model roughness was proposed for DIN standardisation by Sottek & Becker (2019).

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 38455:2024. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-11 | [DIN 38455:2024](https://www.dinmedia.de/en/standard/din-38455/376186532) | current | First edition. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Roughness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html), [Roughness, Daniel & Weber model](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html)

## References

# Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil · **Also known as:** fluctuation strength, vacil, Osses 2016, Fastl and Zwicker fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength describes slow modulation around 4 Hz. Osses, García & Kohlrausch (2016) proposed a signal-based model; Fastl & Zwicker give a closed-form expression for modulated tones and noises. Neither is standardised. ECMA-418-2:2025 added a hearing-model method, listed on its own page.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Osses et al. (2016). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2016 | [Osses et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410) | published | Signal-based model. | — |
| 2007 | [Fastl & Zwicker (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4) | published | Closed-form expression for amplitude- and frequency-modulated sounds. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Fastl, H., & Zwicker, E. (2007). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (3rd ed.). Springer. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-68888-4
2. Osses Vecchi, A., García León, R., & Kohlrausch, A. (2016). Modelling the sensation of fluctuation strength. *Proceedings of Meetings on Acoustics*, 28, 050005. https://doi.org/10.1121/2.0000410

# Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Fluctuation strength · **Unit:** vacil_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 fluctuation strength, vacil_HMS, Sottek fluctuation strength

Fluctuation strength from the Sottek Hearing Model, new in the 4th edition of ECMA-418-2 (June 2025, Clause 9). It uses high-resolution spectral analysis for modulation rates of about 0.25 to 20 Hz.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | New Clause 9. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Fluctuation strength, Osses et al. model and Fastl & Zwicker formula](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/fluctuation-strength-osses.html), [Loudness from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

# Tonality, Aures/Terhardt model

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** t.u. · **Also known as:** Aures tonality, Terhardt tonality, tonality units, t.u., sensory euphony

Tonality from Aures (1985): tonal components are extracted with the method of Terhardt, Stoll & Seewann (1982), weighted, and related to the loudness of the whole sound. Not standardised.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Aures (1985b). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C).

SQAT corrected several issues in September 2026 (for example, only the first tonal component entered the weighting), which changes results compared with SQAT v1.3 and earlier.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | Aures (1985b) | published | Tonality model. | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 1982 | [Terhardt et al. (1982)](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544) | published | Extraction of tonal components used by the model. | — |

## Implementations

| Project | Language | Edition | Functions | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) | Python, C | Aures (1985b) | `tonality_aures` | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop); exact agreement with MATLAB is not established. |

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html)

## References

1. Terhardt, E., Stoll, G., & Seewann, M. (1982). Algorithm for extraction of pitch and pitch salience from complex tonal signals. *The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America*, 71(3), 679–688. https://doi.org/10.1121/1.387544
2. Aures, W. (1985). Berechnungsverfahren für den sensorischen Wohlklang beliebiger Schallsignale [A model for calculating the sensory euphony of various sounds]. *Acustica*, 59, 130–141.

# Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** tu_HMS · **Also known as:** ECMA-418-2 tonality, psychoacoustic tonality, tu_HMS, Sottek tonality, SHM tonality

Psychoacoustic tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model, Clause 6 of ECMA-418-2, with specific tonality and tonal frequency over time. The method came from ECMA-74 (17th edition, 2019) when ECMA-418-2 was first published in 2020.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.). Open-source implementations of it: [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) (Python, C; mono or stereo).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-06 | [ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_4th_edition_june_2025.pdf) | current | Hearing-model and conformance updates (48 kHz sampling). | [MetaSona](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html) |
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | superseded | Further refinement. | — |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Refined calculation. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-2:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-2_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Clause 6 tonality. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Hearing model and tonality before ECMA-418-2 existed. | — |

# Tone-to-noise ratio and prominence ratio (ECMA-418-1)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tone-to-noise-prominence-ratio.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** TNR, PR, ECMA-418-1, ECMA-74 Annex D, prominent discrete tones, ANSI S1.13 Annex

Tone-to-noise ratio (TNR) and prominence ratio (PR) decide whether a discrete tone is prominent: TNR compares the tone with the noise in its critical band, PR compares the critical band with its neighbours. ECMA-418-1 took the method over from Annex D of ECMA-74 in 2020; its 3rd edition (2024) revised the TNR procedure.

**In short.** The current edition is ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf) | current | TNR procedure revised for repeatable results across FFT resolutions; terms rewritten. | — |
| 2022-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2022 (2nd ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf) | superseded | Maximum tone bandwidth for TNR set to 15 % of the critical band; corrections. | — |
| 2020-12 | [ECMA-418-1:2020 (1st ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf) | superseded | Based on, and mostly identical to, ECMA-74 Annex D. | — |
| 2019-12 | [ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.)](https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/) | superseded | Annex D, before ECMA-418-1 existed. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Tonality from the Sottek Hearing Model (ECMA-418-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html), [Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html)

## References

1. ECMA-74:2019 (17th ed.). Measurement of airborne noise emitted by information technology and telecommunications equipment. https://ecma-international.org/publications-and-standards/standards/ecma-74/
2. ECMA-418-1:2020 (1st ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_1st_edition_december_2020.pdf
3. ECMA-418-1:2022 (2nd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_2nd_edition_december_2022.pdf
4. ECMA-418-1:2024 (3rd ed.). Psychoacoustic metrics for ITT equipment — Part 1 (prominent discrete tones). https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-418-1_3rd_edition_december_2024.pdf

# Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** DIN 45681, tone adjustment, K_T, Tonzuschlag

German method that detects tonal components in noise from narrow-band spectra and derives a tone adjustment for the assessment of noise immissions. DIN 45681:2005 with its corrections of 2005 and 2006 is current.

**In short.** The current edition is DIN 45681:2005. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

# Audibility of tones in noise (ISO/TS 20065)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-20065.html

**Quantity:** Tonality · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/TS 20065, ISO/PAS 20065, tonal audibility, decisive audibility, ΔL_ta

Engineering method for the audibility of tones in noise, from critical-band analysis of narrow-band spectra. First published as ISO/PAS 20065:2016 and turned into ISO/TS 20065:2022, which notes that the method is not validated below 50 Hz.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO/TS 20065:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-12 | [ISO/TS 20065:2022](https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html) | current | Technical specification; adds that the method is not validated below 50 Hz. | — |
| 2016-07 | [ISO/PAS 20065:2016](https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html) | withdrawn | Publicly available specification; withdrawn in 2022. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

**See also:** [Tonal components and tone adjustment (DIN 45681)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-din-45681.html), [Tonal audibility in environmental noise (ISO 1996-2)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonal-audibility-iso-1996-2.html)

## References

1. ISO/PAS 20065:2016. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/66941.html
2. ISO/TS 20065:2022. Acoustics — Objective method for assessing the audibility of tones in noise — Engineering method. https://www.iso.org/standard/81518.html

Objective tonal audibility and tone adjustment for environmental noise assessment. ISO 1996-2:2007 gave a method in Annex C; ISO 1996-2:2017 replaced it with an engineering method (Annex J) and a survey method (Annex K).

# Prominence of impulsive sounds (ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/impulsiveness.html

**Quantity:** Impulsiveness · **Unit:** dB · **Also known as:** ISO/PAS 1996-3, NT ACOU 112, impulsiveness, impulse adjustment, impulsive sound prominence

Objective prominence of impulsive sounds and the corresponding adjustment of the equivalent level in environmental noise assessment: Nordtest method NT ACOU 112 and ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022 (adjustment of 0 to 9 dB). Hearing-model impulsiveness metrics are not standardised and no open implementation is listed.

**In short.** The current edition is ISO/PAS 1996-3:2022. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2002-05 | NT ACOU 112 | current | Nordic test method. | — |

# Psychoacoustic annoyance (Widmann, Zwicker & Fastl, More, Di et al.)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html

**Quantity:** Psychoacoustic annoyance · **Unit:** dimensionless · **Also known as:** PA, psychoacoustic annoyance, Zwicker annoyance, Widmann annoyance, More annoyance, Di annoyance

Psychoacoustic annoyance (PA) combines percentile loudness N5 with sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength (Widmann 1992; Zwicker & Fastl 1999). More (2010) added tonality and Di et al. (2016) adapted the model for tonal noise. None of these is standardised; ISO/AWI 26573, registered in 2026, covers the assessment of annoyance through listening tests, including prediction models.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference models are Widmann (1992), Zwicker & Fastl (1999), More (2010), and Di et al. (2016). In development: ISO/AWI 26573. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04 | [ISO/AWI 26573](https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html) | in development | Approved work item (stage 20.00) since 2026. | — |
| 2016 | [Di et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006) | published | Adapted for tonal noise. | — |
| 2010 | More (2010) | published | Adds tonality. | — |
| 1999 | Zwicker & Fastl (1999) | published | Book version of the model. | — |
| 1992 | Widmann (1992) | published | Original model. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

## References

1. Widmann, U. (1992). *Ein Modell der psychoakustischen Lästigkeit von Schallen und seine Anwendung in der Praxis der Lärmbeurteilung* [Doctoral dissertation, Technische Universität München].
2. Zwicker, E., & Fastl, H. (1999). *Psychoacoustics: Facts and models* (2nd ed.). Springer.
3. More, S. R. (2010). *Aircraft noise characteristics and metrics* [Doctoral dissertation, Purdue University]. PARTNER report PARTNER-COE-2011-004.
4. Di, G., Chen, X., Song, K., Zhou, B., & Pei, C. (2016). Improvement of Zwicker's psychoacoustic annoyance model aiming at tonal noises. *Applied Acoustics*, 105, 164–170. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apacoust.2015.12.006
5. ISO/AWI 26573. Acoustics — Procedures for assessment and prediction of noise-induced perceptual annoyance through laboratory-based listening tests. https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html

# Equal-loudness-level contours (ISO 226)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/equal-loudness-contours.html

Normal equal-loudness-level contours for pure tones in free-field listening. ISO 226:2023 replaced ISO 226:2003; ECMA-418-2:2025 still refers to the 2003 edition.

# Perceived noise level, PNLT and EPNL (ICAO Annex 16, 14 CFR Part 36)

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/epnl.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** PNdB, EPNdB · **Also known as:** EPNL, EPNdB, PNL, PNLT, perceived noisiness, noy, aircraft noise certification

Effective perceived noise level for aircraft noise certification: perceived noisiness in noy, the tone-corrected perceived noise level (PNLT) and a duration correction. Defined in ICAO Annex 16, Volume I, and in the US regulation 14 CFR Part 36.

**In short.** The current edition is ICAO Annex 16, Vol. I and 14 CFR Part 36. No open-source implementation of it has been found.

# Aural detectability of sounds in background noise

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/aural-detectability.html

**Quantity:** Related quantities · **Unit:** d′ (detectability index), dB · **Also known as:** detectability, d-prime, signal detection, aural detection, audibility of aircraft

How likely a listener is to detect a sound in background noise, from signal-to-noise ratios in auditory filters and signal-detection theory. Used for aircraft, drone and urban air mobility noise. Not standardised.

**In short.** There is no standard; the reference model is Fidell et al. (1974). No open-source implementation of it has been found.

## Editions and who implements them

| Date | Edition | Status | What changed | Implemented by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1974 | [Fidell et al. (1974)](https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405) | published | Model paper. | — |

## Implementations

No open-source implementation has been found yet. If you know one, please [open an issue](https://github.com/ZhenxianLi/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/issues/new/choose).

## References

1. Fidell, S., Pearsons, K. S., & Bennett, R. (1974). Prediction of aural detectability of noise signals. *Human Factors*, 16(4), 373–383. https://doi.org/10.1177/001872087401600405

# MetaSona

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/projects/metasona.html

C library with a typed Python interface and prebuilt wheels, written to make repeated psychoacoustic analysis fast. Covers Zwicker loudness, DIN 45692 sharpness, Daniel–Weber roughness, Aures tonality and ECMA-418-2:2025 loudness, roughness and tonality.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona
- **Documentation:** https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/docs/python-api.md
- **Language:** Python, C
- **Kind:** Library
- **Licence:** GPL-3.0-only AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause AND MIT — The combined distribution is GPL-3.0; MetaSona's own code keeps Apache-2.0 and the adapted SQAT, MoSQITo and PocketFFT parts keep their BSD-3-Clause, MIT or Apache-2.0 notices.
- **Package:** PyPI `metasona` (https://pypi.org/project/metasona/)
- **Install:** `pip install metasona`
- **Latest release:** 0.2.2 (2026-09)
- **Last commit:** 2026-09-25 (active)
- **Maintainers:** Jiahua Zhang
- **AI assistance:** disclosed — README and NOTICE state that it was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex.
- **Entry checked:** 2026-10-06

## What it implements

| Metric | Edition | Functions | Status | Validation (as stated) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Zwicker loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-zwicker.html) | ISO 532-1:2017 — stationary and time-varying; also from 28 third-octave levels | `stationary_loudness`, `time_varying_loudness`, `loudness_from_levels` | available | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Model tables taken from MoSQITo and checked element by element; one upper-slope value (0.22) follows the ISO 532-1 reference C table where MoSQITo uses 0.24. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model loudness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/loudness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) — Clause 8 loudness with tonal/noise separation; mono or stereo | `loudness_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | another implementation | since 0.2.0; Adapted from the SQAT/RefMap MATLAB code by Lotinga and Torjussen. |
| [Sharpness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/sharpness.html) | DIN 45692:2009 — from specific loudness | `sharpness_din45692` | available | not stated | since 0.1.0 |
| [Roughness (Daniel & Weber)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-daniel-weber.html) | Daniel & Weber (1997) | `roughness_daniel_weber` | available | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Follows SQAT revision `e6228b78`, which includes SQAT's September 2026 rewrite. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model roughness](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/roughness-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) — mono or stereo; optional entropy weighting not applied | `roughness_ecma` | available | another implementation | since 0.2.0; Uses the standard's 20 ms grid and nominal calibration factor, where SQAT uses a slightly adjusted calibration. |
| [Tonality (Aures)](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-aures.html) | Aures (1985b) | `tonality_aures` | available | another implementation | since 0.1.0; Follows SQAT's September 2026 revision (250 ms Hann windows, 125 ms hop); exact agreement with MATLAB is not established. |
| [Sottek Hearing Model tonality](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/tonality-ecma-418-2.html) | ECMA-418-2:2025 (4th ed.) — mono or stereo | `tonality_ecma`, `ecma_tonal_analysis` | available | another implementation | since 0.2.0 |

## Notes

- First commit and first PyPI release on 2026-09-16.
- Ports a pinned SQAT revision (`e6228b78`, after SQAT's September 2026 fixes) and model data from MoSQITo; differences to both are listed in [THIRD_PARTY.md](https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md).
- Expects calibrated pressure in pascals. The Python interface resamples to 48 kHz; the C functions require 48 kHz.
- The README reports speed-ups over MoSQITo 1.2.1 (e.g. 73× for time-varying loudness on its benchmark signal).

## Before you rely on it

- The README calls the current version experimental, particularly roughness and tonality, and says standards conformance has not been established.
- Comparisons with SQAT and MoSQITo are described as kept outside the package repository, and the third-party notes say exact agreement with the MATLAB code is not established.

## Sources

- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/README.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY.md
- https://github.com/huaaudio/metasona/blob/main/NOTICE
- https://pypi.org/project/metasona/

# Standards and models

> Part of the [Psychoacoustic Metrics Index](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/), an index of open-source implementations of psychoacoustic metrics. Data as of 2026-10-06. Web page: https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/standards.html

Every document the index refers to, newest first. Each implementation in the index is tied to one of these editions.

## Standards and regulations

| Date | Document | Title | Status | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-04 | [ISO/AWI 26573](https://www.iso.org/standard/93922.html) | Acoustics — Procedures for assessment and prediction of noise-induced perceptual annoyance through laboratory-based listening tests | in development | [Psychoacoustic annoyance](https://zhenxianli.github.io/psychoacoustic-metrics-index/metrics/psychoacoustic-annoyance.html) |
